title: IATA General Conditions of Carriage Articles 8 and 12 — Wrongful Refusal of Carriage and Breach of Carriage Conditions
category: International Aviation / Human Rights / Treaty Law

incident.location: Santiago International Airport (SCL), aboard aircraft LA8159, Chile

allegation_summary: LATAM Airlines Brazil (TAM Linhas Aéreas)' refusal to carry passenger [[SPK-passenger-leandro]] on flight LA8159 violated the IATA General Conditions of Carriage (Resolution 724), which form part of the contract of carriage between the airline and passenger. Article 8.1 permits refusal of carriage only on specified grounds (safety, conduct causing hazard or discomfort to others, failure to follow crew instructions, improper documentation, etc.). None of these grounds existed in fact — as proven by PDI CCTV disproving the aggression allegation. The carrier's reliance on a false and unverified allegation of 'conduct' does not satisfy the Article 8.1 standard which requires 'reasonable discretion.' Furthermore, the removal was procedurally defective: the carrier failed to follow its own Conditions regarding documentation (Article 3), the ticket as prima facie evidence of contract, and the passenger's right to carriage absent lawful grounds for refusal.

articles.article_text: Any clause contained in the contract of carriage and all special agreements entered into before the damage occurred by which the parties purport to infringe the rules laid down by this Convention, whether by deciding the law to be applied, or by altering the rules as to jurisdiction, shall be null and void.
